result.rationale: Verifiable in the diff: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50), totalPages = 3 while only 2 pages of members exist. Compounding it, the next action sets offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count), which yields offset = 100 = user_count, so findMembers requests an empty page 3 and currentPage (Math.floor(offset/limit)+1) = 3 equals totalPages, making showingLast true on a page with zero members — a real phantom-page defect introduced by this diff.

judged_text: Pagination off-by-one: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing a phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

record.issue_text: Pagination off-by-one: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing a phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100/50), this returns 3 instead of 2, so `showingLast` (propertyEqual currentPage/totalPages) stays false on the real last page and the `next` action can advance `offset` to `user_count`, leading `findMembers()` to request an empty page (`offset` becomes `user_count`). Using `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` would avoid the phantom last page.
